# Task 4A — Few-Shot Prompting: Additional Quiz Samples

**Technique:** Few-shot prompting (2 examples provided, 2 generated by Copilot).

**Objective:** Standardize the "Spot the Scam" quiz item format so every sample has the same structure: pattern name, three red flags, and a plain-language explanation.

---

## Exact Prompt Submitted

> I am building the “Spot the Scam” quiz for the Scam Shield page. Use this exact format for each sample:
>
> **Example 1:**  
> Pattern: Fake GCash refund SMS  
> Red Flags: (1) Unsolicited link, (2) “Expires bukas” urgency, (3) Sender is not the official GCash shortcode.  
> Explanation: GCash and banks will never ask you to click a link to “claim” a refund. Open the GCash app directly if you want to check your account.
>
> **Example 2:**  
> Pattern: Fake SSS app download link  
> Red Flags: (1) Caller pressures you to install an app during the call, (2) Link does not go to Google Play or Apple App Store, (3) Caller asks you to stay on the line while installing.  
> Explanation: Government agencies do not call and ask you to install apps through links. Download official apps only from the official store.
>
> Generate **two additional** educational samples in the same format. One should model a fake DSWD ayuda SMS; the other should model a fake “failed delivery” parcel SMS. Render all four samples in the quiz using the same HTML card structure already in `index.html`.

---

## Actual Copilot Output (samples generated)

### Sample 3 — Fake DSWD ayuda SMS

- **Pattern:** Fake DSWD ayuda SMS
- **Red Flags:**
  1. Promises a specific peso amount in an unsolicited text message.
  2. Link is not a `dswd.gov.ph` domain.
  3. Creates urgency with a same-day deadline (“forfeited bukas”).
- **Explanation:** DSWD does not distribute ayuda through links in text messages. Verify announcements through your barangay or the official DSWD page.

### Sample 4 — Fake failed-delivery parcel SMS

- **Pattern:** Fake failed-delivery parcel SMS
- **Red Flags:**
  1. You are not expecting a parcel.
  2. Link asks for personal information or a “redelivery fee.”
  3. Sender is an unknown mobile number.
- **Explanation:** Legitimate couriers do not ask for payment through an SMS link. Track your parcel only through the courier’s official app or website.

---

## What Worked

- All four samples now share the same structural depth: one pattern name, exactly three red flags, and one plain-language explanation.
- Rendering was inserted into the existing `<article class="quiz-card">` structure without breaking the quiz button layout.
- Content uses local agencies (DSWD, GCash, SSS) rather than generic international examples.

## What Needs Improvement

- Copilot did not verify local domain details. In the generated DSWD sample, one draft variant included a fabricated agency URL that I removed before applying the output to `index.html`. Few-shot prompting improves **format consistency**, not **factual accuracy**.
- The generated samples are still labeled "Educational Example Only" in the HTML, but the few-shot prompt itself did not enforce the label — I had to add it during manual review.

## Next Action / Verification

- Inspect all four rendered cards in the browser to confirm structural uniformity.
- Confirm every sample has a visible "Educational Example Only" label — required by the structured-prompt constraints from Task 3.
- Cross-check each red flag against official agency guidance (CICC, DSWD, GCash, SSS) before considering the content production-ready.
